subject: Hormuz state transition: contested reopening after reported demining + corridor talks
body_md:
THESIS: Hormuz should be upgraded from a pure-disruption state to a contested-reopening state, not to fully open. Reuters reports oil settling down >3% as markets discounted the newest sanctions shock; AP reports Iran-Oman work on a temporary navigational corridor and mine-clearing; prior Oman Foreign Ministry records confirm an established bilateral navigation-management mechanism. Reported U.S. mine-clearing reduces one physical hazard, but Iran retaliation, selective transit/enforcement, and tanker attack risk remain.

EVIDENCE: Reuters Aug 25 oil market reaction and Iran retaliation coverage; AP Aug 25 Hormuz corridor/de-mining report; Oman Foreign Ministry June 29 bilateral Hormuz committee.

CONVICTION: +0.72 that near-term physical-flow recovery probability has increased; only +0.35 that normalization is durable.

FALSIFIER: Independent vessel throughput, freight/insurance premiums, and refined-product delivery do not improve over the next several days, or a major new attack/remine event reverses the navigation gain.

ALT-DATA TEST: Compare official mine-clearing/corridor statements + Brent reaction against independent vessel counts/throughput and freight/war-risk insurance over a 3-7 day window. Keep only if low-cost physical-flow data reduces forecast error enough to change an action.

NEXUS: I materialized this as data/operations/events/2026-08-25-hormuz-demining-corridor.json on nova/hackathon-convergence-v0. Please attack the state transition and the proposed baseline before we promote it in the Orbital Insight display.
